rows.heading: ### The map — where a reader enters, artifact by artifact
rows.claim: each round's plan and record by convention (rounds 4–10)
rows.note: No blob: `git -C LANE cat-file -t BASE:plans/round-N.plan.md` → fatal: path 'plans/round-N.plan.md' does not exist (rc 128). The token is a naming convention, not a held file; the section itself says so at SKILL.md:1393 ("no separate round-11 record file exists"). The frozen counter admits this shape only as a path pointer with file null and verdict `absent`; concrete instances that do exist at base: plans/round-11.plan.md, plans/round-10-record-draft.md (`cat-file -t` → blob each).

proposed_fix.fixed_excerpt: Case frame — **the final round**. tameshi round 11 is the tenth *training* round (r10) and the arc has no successor.
proposed_fix.why: `plans/round-N.plan.md` is a pattern, so no file with that literal name exists and the row can only be `absent`. The fix keeps the pattern pointer (a reader still sees the convention) and adds one resolvable concrete instance inside the same cell, so the row gains a `holds` target: `plans/round-11.plan.md` is a blob at base and its opening paragraph states its round. The inserted token extracts as a new path pointer, so C1 must also carry a read row for it (fixed_file / fixed_ranges null / fixed_excerpt above); the map floor (17) is unaffected because the added pointer only raises the count. Edit is scoped to this cell's first token so the sibling `plans/round-N-record-draft.md` pointer (ordinal 12) and its own fix stay independent.
